key_insight: Riordan arrays could provide an algebraic inductive bias for AI through structured causal linear transformations of sequences.
engineering_relevance: These operators may enable parameter-efficient sequence layers, interpretable recurrent systems, and invertible architectures for hierarchical data.
method: Represent a data sequence by its generating function A(z).
Apply the Riordan transformation A(z) → g(z)A(f(z)).
Explore structured architectures combining convolution, substitution, and multiscale mixing.
evidence_signal: The abstract proposes architectures and an initial experimental program but reports no datasets, benchmarks, or measured results.
watch_item: Practical implementations must address finite truncation and numerical behavior; the infinite-dimensional formulation alone does not establish effectiveness.
paper_title: Riordan Arrays as Structured Operators for Artificial Intelligence
